landing.scienceQuote: Impulsive decisions under volatility consistently lead to worse outcomes.
landing.scienceDesc: Behavioral finance research shows that emotional reactions — panic selling during drops, euphoric buying during surges — are among the most reliable predictors of poor returns. A brief pause before action leads to better decisions.
landing.scienceStepsIntro: Each step in Holzen's pause session follows a specific principle from clinical and behavioral research:
landing.scienceStepBreathe: Activate your parasympathetic nervous system. Slowing your breath shifts your body from fight-or-flight to a regulated state where clear thinking becomes possible.
landing.scienceStepFeel: Label what you're experiencing. Putting feelings into words ('affect labeling') reduces amygdala activation — but only after arousal has been lowered first.
landing.scienceStepReflect: Engage in cognitive reappraisal. Reframing a situation after emotional regulation leads to better decision-making than suppression or avoidance.
landing.scienceStepShift: Notice what changed. Checking in after reflection creates metacognitive awareness — the ability to observe your own thinking, which is key to self-regulation.
landing.scienceStepDecide: Act from intention, not impulse. System 2 is now online: you've moved from reactive to deliberate processing.
landing.scienceStepsSummary: Regulate your nervous system, label your emotions, reframe the situation, observe what shifted, then decide deliberately. Each step is backed by peer-reviewed research from Porges, Lieberman, Gross, Flavell, and Kahneman.
landing.pricingDesc: {{freeReflectionsPerMonth}} pauses per month — free forever, no credit card. Or start a {{trialDays}}-day free trial of Pro (${{price}}/month after): unlimited pauses, AI companions, insights, library, and more. Cancel anytime.

faq.whoAnswer: Anyone who holds Bitcoin and has ever felt the urge to sell during a crash or buy during a surge. Holzen is for holders who want to understand their emotional patterns — not traders looking for signals.
faq.breatheQuestion: I don't need an app to tell me to breathe.
faq.breatheAnswer: You're right — you don't. But Holzen doesn't just remind you to breathe. It intercepts you at the exact moment volatility hits, sequences you through a science-backed protocol (regulate → label → reappraise → decide), and tracks your patterns over time. Willpower alone doesn't build a practice. Timing and structure do.
faq.meditationQuestion: Isn't this just another meditation app?
faq.meditationAnswer: Meditation apps are general-purpose. Holzen is triggered by real market events — it meets you in the moment you're most likely to act on impulse. It combines breathing, AI reflections, behavioral science, curated intelligence, and long-term pattern tracking into one practice. Calm doesn't know when Bitcoin just dropped 8%.
faq.valueQuestion: ${{price}}/month for something I might rarely use?
faq.valueAnswer:
The moments you use Holzen are the moments that matter most — when a single impulsive decision can cost thousands. One avoided panic sell or FOMO buy pays for years of the subscription.

How often you pause is not "once in a blue moon" by design: when markets are choppy or your thresholds are sensitive, alerts can add up to many times a month. In settings, Holzen estimates how often you would have paused on recent price action so you can tune how often you want to be interrupted instead of guessing. You can also request a pause anytime from Home without waiting for an alert, with a short cooldown so the habit stays intentional.

And the free tier gives you {{freeReflectionsPerMonth}} pauses per month forever.
faq.fairUseAnswer: Pro includes unlimited pauses and AI companions for personal use — there's no per-month cap you can hit. To keep the service healthy for everyone, we apply light technical limits (a short cooldown between pauses and a per-hour ceiling) that real users never notice in practice. These only come into play for clearly abusive patterns like scripted traffic or repeated automated runs.
faq.worksAnswer: Each step follows peer-reviewed research: vagal breathing (Porges), affect labeling (Lieberman), cognitive reappraisal (Gross), metacognition (Flavell), and deliberate decision-making (Kahneman). Over time, your stats reveal patterns you can't see in the moment — and that awareness itself shifts behavior.
faq.rationalQuestion: I'm a long-term holder — I don't panic.
faq.rationalAnswer: That's what most holders believe until a -20% day. Research shows even experienced investors overestimate their emotional resilience. Holzen isn't just for panic — it catches subtle patterns like over-checking, quiet anxiety, or euphoric overconfidence that erode conviction without you noticing.
faq.dataQuestion: What happens to my emotional data?
faq.dataAnswer: We store only what's needed: your email, thresholds, pauses, and mood entries. You can export everything as JSON or CSV anytime, or delete your account entirely with one tap. See our

landing.footer: Holzen is not a trading tool. It won't tell you what to do. It exists to help you understand yourself — one volatile moment at a time.

about.opportunityBody1: The democratisation of investing is one of the most important financial shifts of our time.
about.opportunityBody2: Platforms like Robinhood, Trade Republic, and countless others have opened markets that were once reserved for professionals. Anyone can now invest in stocks, ETFs, commodities — and Bitcoin. This is a genuinely good thing.
about.opportunityBody3: But access is only half the equation. What these platforms don't provide is the emotional infrastructure to handle what comes next: the volatility, the uncertainty, the constant temptation to act when doing nothing would serve you better.
about.opportunityBody4: That's the gap Holzen fills — not with more data or faster alerts, but with a practice of self-awareness designed to create space between impulse and decision.
about.researchBody1: Investing is hard. Controlling your emotions under volatility is harder.
about.researchBody2: Behavioral finance has spent decades documenting this. Daniel Kahneman's work on System 1 and System 2 thinking shows that under stress, our fast, instinctive mind hijacks decisions before our slower, reflective mind can intervene. Barber and Odean's research found that the most active individual traders underperform by 6.5% annually — not because they lack information, but because they act on emotion.
about.researchBody3: This is true for experienced investors and beginners alike. The difference is that beginners often don't yet recognise the pattern: the urge to sell when prices fall, the urge to buy when prices surge. Both feel rational in the moment. Neither usually is.
about.researchBody4: Holzen applies this research directly. When volatility crosses your threshold, you're guided through a science-backed pause designed to move you from reactive to deliberate.
about.pauseResearchTitle: The science behind the five-step pause
about.pauseResearchIntro: Every pause session follows a sequence grounded in clinical and behavioral research — not guesswork.
about.pauseResearchBreatheDesc: Slow, rhythmic breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, shifting your body from fight-or-flight to a regulated state. Polyvagal Theory (Porges, 2011) shows this is a prerequisite for clear thinking.
about.pauseResearchFeelDesc: Labeling your emotions — what researchers call 'affect labeling' — reduces amygdala activation. Lieberman et al. (2007) found this works best after physiological arousal has been lowered first.
about.pauseResearchReflectDesc: Cognitive reappraisal — reframing the situation — leads to better decisions than suppression. Gross (2002) showed that reappraisal is most effective once emotional intensity has been reduced.
about.pauseResearchShiftDesc: Checking in again after reflection builds metacognitive awareness — the ability to observe your own thinking patterns, identified by Flavell (1979) as key to self-regulation.
about.pauseResearchDecideDesc: With your nervous system regulated and emotions labeled, Kahneman's System 2 (2011) is online. You can now act from intention rather than impulse.
about.readFullScience: See the full research on our landing page →
about.bitcoinBody1: Holding Bitcoin is especially hard — and we think that's exactly why it's worth doing.
about.bitcoinBody2: Bitcoin behaves like a volatile tech stock in the short term, but we believe it is something fundamentally different: the best savings technology ever invented. A decentralised, scarce, programmable monetary network with no counterparty risk.
about.bitcoinBody3: We believe Bitcoin represents the most asymmetric bet in the history of financial markets. But capturing that asymmetry requires one thing above all else: the ability to hold through volatility.
about.bitcoinBody4: Holzen exists to help people hold — with awareness. We don't tell you what to do. We help you pause long enough to notice your impulse, name it, and choose deliberately.
about.philosophyBody1: Holzen is a micropreneur project — small by design.
about.philosophyBody2: We don't have investors, a growth team, or a roadmap optimised for scale. We have a focused product, a clear price, and users who value what we build.
about.philosophyBody3: We believe the best software is often built by small teams who care deeply about the problem they're solving. No engagement metrics, no dark patterns, no pressure to grow at all costs.
about.reserveBody1: We hold what we help others hold.
about.reserveBody2: Holzen maintains a Bitcoin reserve as a long-term store of value — not as speculation, but as a statement of conviction.
about.aboutUsBody1: Holzen is built by a husband-and-wife team. We're Bitcoin holders ourselves, and we built this tool because we needed it.
about.aboutUsBody2: We hope Holzen can do the same for you.

reserve.title: BTC Reserve Strategy
reserve.subtitle: We hold what we help others hold.
reserve.whyWeHoldBody1: A product that helps people hold Bitcoin should itself hold Bitcoin. Anything else would be a contradiction.
reserve.whyWeHoldBody2: Holzen maintains a Bitcoin reserve — not as a financial strategy, but as a statement of conviction. We believe Bitcoin is the best savings technology ever created.
reserve.whyWeHoldBody3: Our reserve is denominated in Bitcoin, not dollars. We don't measure success by fiat returns. We measure it by the discipline of not selling.
reserve.strategyBody: We allocate a significant portion of company treasury to Bitcoin. We acquire through dollar-cost averaging and opportunistic buys during periods of elevated fear. We do not trade. We do not hedge. We do not lend.
reserve.reserveNotStarted: Our reserve hasn't started yet. When it does, the numbers will appear here — transparent from the first sat.
reserve.convictionBody1: Our approach is inspired by companies like MicroStrategy, who demonstrated that a corporate Bitcoin reserve isn't speculative — it's a statement about the future of money.
reserve.convictionBody2: Every sat in our treasury represents the same conviction we ask our users to practice. We don't just build tools for holders — we are holders.
reserve.closingQuote: The practice is the same whether you hold 0.001 BTC or 10,000. Sit with the volatility. Notice the impulse. Choose deliberately.

pauseScience.title: Each step follows research
pauseScience.breatheDesc: Slow breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, shifting from fight-or-flight to regulation. (Porges, 2011)
pauseScience.feelDesc: Labeling emotions ('affect labeling') reduces amygdala activation — but only after arousal is lowered. (Lieberman et al., 2007)
pauseScience.reflectDesc: Cognitive reappraisal after regulation leads to better decisions than suppression. (Gross, 2002)
pauseScience.shiftDesc: Checking in again builds metacognitive awareness — observing your own thinking. (Flavell, 1979)
pauseScience.decideDesc: System 2 is now online. You can act from intention, not impulse. (Kahneman, 2011)
